subject: Materials Science
title: Crevice Corrosion: Trapped and Attacked
description: A micro-lesson that makes Crevice Corrosion: Trapped and Attacked usable.

hook.text: Under a gasket or between overlapping plates, stagnant water creates a corrosion trap.

buildup.text: Crevice corrosion occurs in narrow gaps where electrolyte stagnates and oxygen depletes.

discovery.text: Low oxygen inside the crevice makes it the anode — the open surface becomes the cathode and stays protected.

twist.text: Even stainless steel pits badly in crevices — the passive film can't survive without oxygen to repair itself.

climax.text: Engineers eliminate crevices by welding instead of bolting, and by sealing joints with corrosion-resistant compounds.

punchline.text: The tightest gaps cause the worst corrosion — trapped water always wins.

quiz.question: What causes crevice corrosion?
options: High flow velocity eroding the surface
Oxygen depletion in stagnant electrolyte within narrow gaps
Ultraviolet light degrading the metal surface
